body:
Applicable behaviour: the observation (state-change-feed) cursor is a GLOBAL, filter-independent durable commit position — a ledger-wide change sequence — not a per-subscription position.

Why the question even arises: exactly one local source states the opposite. docs/engineering/notes/cursor-note.md claims "cursor positions are per-subscription, not global." That note is self-labelled "informational, not normative" and explicitly "was not updated against the current pinned artifact."

Resolution rule (local, no peer needed): docs/engineering/08-source-precedence-policy.md (PLMP-ALN-2) — (1) "The published contract of the exact pinned version (its shipped type declarations and release specification) governs that interface's behaviour"; (3) informational records "are explanatory only and never override 1 or 2." The note falls under (3); the pinned contract falls under (1).

Exact pinned version: @ordarium/core, @ordarium/host-kit, @ordarium/ledger-sqlite pinned to ordarium-v1.3.1 in package.json and pnpm-workspace.yaml overrides, and installed under node_modules/@ordarium/* at 1.3.1. (docs/engineering/07, whose last revision entries stop at 1.2.0, is a historical alignment record, i.e. informational for version currency; it does not address the observation cursor.)

Pinned-contract evidence that governs:
- @ordarium/core 1.3.1 types.d.ts: StateChangePage.cursor = "Opaque, filter-independent durable position of the last delivered change"; unlike other read surfaces, for the change feed "cursor is always present"; StateChangeFilter.namespace only "restrict[s] observation to one namespace" and "absent observes every namespace."
- @ordarium/core 1.3.1 ledger.js (MemoryLedger.changes): positions are contiguous 1..n over all commits; cursor = base64url({"c":"<position>"}); a position beyond the ledger's own history throws InvalidCursorError.
- @ordarium/ledger-sqlite 1.3.1 index.js changes(): "the cursor is a global, filter-independent position, so this compares against the whole ledger, not the requested namespace's last sequence"; validation is `after > #stateChangeHighWater()` -> InvalidCursorError; rows are ordered by the ledger-wide `change_seq`.
- @ordarium/ledger-sqlite 1.3.1 migrations.d.ts (schema v4): "v3 recorded no global commit order ... From v4 on, every new commit carries the real durable database order."
- @ordarium/core 1.3.1 errors.d.ts InvalidCursorError: a caller-supplied change-feed cursor that is not a durable position fails closed, "instead of silently restarting from the beginning of the feed."

Consequences for this integration: a cursor returned by changes() is ledger-wide and reusable across different namespace filters; it cannot be treated as an independent per-subscription offset (two namespace-scoped "subscriptions" cannot each own the returned value). Foreign/restored/corrupt cursors fail closed rather than restarting. This governs the state-change-feed surface whenever the integration consumes it; note the workspace consumes only list()/listStates (subject-ordered pagination) for telemetry load and does not currently call changes() (no `.changes(` in src), so this is a contract-level determination, not a change to existing code. It is also distinct from Palimpsest's own EventCursor/ViewCursor distinction (docs/engineering/35), which concerns canonical event positions, not the Ordarium observation cursor.

The stale note should not be relied on; if it is retained it should be marked superseded for the pinned 1.3.1 line.
